ordered_diagnoses: Intrauterine pregnancy with methimazole-induced hCG elevation

facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks
A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

concepts.why: The patient had a negative point-of-care urine hCG test, but a subsequent serum hCG test showed a high level, and ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy, suggesting a possible heterotopic pregnancy.

concepts.preferred_label: Intrauterine pregnancy with methimazole-induced hCG elevation
concepts.why: The patient was prescribed methimazole, which can cause an elevation in hCG levels, and she had a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, which could explain the high serum hCG level.
The patient had a history of thyroid condition, undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone, and a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, which could be consistent with Graves' disease.

rationales.F09: Negative POC hCG test does not rule out pregnancy due to potential false negative
